NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical nexus of AI infrastructure, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that is almost entirely dependent on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and SK Hynix/Samsung for HBM memory, creating concentrated upstream risk. Downstream, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a handful of hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who collectively represent the majority of its data center GPU demand, making it both a key enabler and a potential bottleneck of the global AI buildout.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a fabless designer of proprietary silicon and a systems integrator reliant on a concentrated network of Asian semiconductor and display manufacturers — most critically TSMC — for component production. On the downstream side, Apple distributes through major U.S. and global wireless carriers and retailers, while its high-margin Services segment creates a unique digital ecosystem dependency with partners like Alphabet, making Apple both a product seller and platform operator.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC occupies the most critical chokepoint in the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, manufacturing chips designed by fabless companies and IDMs across virtually every end market including mobile, AI, HPC, automotive, and IoT. The company is uniquely dependent on a concentrated set of Western equipment suppliers — particularly ASML for irreplaceable EUV lithography — while simultaneously serving as an indispensable manufacturing partner for the world's most valuable technology companies, giving TSMC both significant leverage and significant geopolitical exposure.

On the downstream side, IREN monetizes its operations primarily through Bitcoin market sales via exchanges like Coinbase, while increasingly targeting enterprise AI/HPC customers to lease GPU compute capacity, diversifying revenue beyond pure crypto mining.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo occupies an early-stage, vertically ambitious position in the advanced fission value chain, sitting between specialized nuclear fuel enrichers and fabricators upstream (critically dependent on HALEU availability) and a diverse set of power-hungry industrial and data center customers downstream. The company's commercial viability is heavily contingent on NRC licensing milestones, securing a reliable HALEU fuel supply chain that is still nascent at industrial scale, and converting its letter-of-intent pipeline—including the marquee Microsoft partnership—into binding power purchase agreements as Aurora powerhouses move toward deployment.
